checks.result: Not enforced. findStateFiles accepts a candidate with fs.existsSync(p) only (hooks/stilo-state.js:87 upward walk, :108 one-level scan). existsSync follows symlinks, so a symlinked .stilo directory or state.json is accepted as long as the target exists. The one-level scan skips symlinked subdirectories (Dirent.isDirectory at :105), but it does not check the .stilo component or the state.json leaf. resolveProjeto (:278-294) then passes the lexical link path to readStateResult (:132, fs.readFileSync, which also follows links) and stores it as statePath. No lstat, realpath, containment check or isFile check exists on this path. The only sibling with a file-type check is stilo-diagnostics.js#fileCheck (statSync().isFile(), which follows links and is not wired into the hooks). No hook calls writeJsonAtomic/writeState.

candidates.title: Injected 'fix/write .stilo/state.json' directives can steer the agent to overwrite a user file outside the project through a repository-planted symlink
candidates.description: A third-party repository can ship .stilo/state.json (or the .stilo directory) as a symlink to a file outside the project. Examples are a JSON config such as ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.docker/config.json, which lands in the 'invalid' branch, or any non-JSON dotfile, which lands in the 'unreadable' branch. Discovery accepts the link because fs.existsSync follows it. The hooks then inject a protected plugin-state block that names the in-project link path as the 'Arquivo'. The block tells the agent, as high-authority plugin instructions, that it must correct all fields of state.json (invalid) or fix the file (unreadable) before doing anything else. Every subsequent prompt repeats 'não avance nem aja até corrigir o arquivo'. The valid branch also tells the agent to write the next phase into .stilo/state.json. If the agent's write tool follows the link, the user's file outside the project is overwritten or edited with Stilo state JSON. The agent's tool-permission system is the only remaining gate.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Neither hooks/stilo-state.js#findStateFiles nor resolveProjeto checks the identity of the discovered state path before blocoEstado/buildStateLine tell the agent to write or repair it. There is no lstat or no-follow check on the .stilo component or the state.json leaf, no realpath containment inside the project directory and no isFile check. Discovery uses only fs.existsSync, which follows links. The injected text then shows the unresolved link path, so the agent and the user cannot see that the write target lies outside the project.

trace.description: resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) runs on the opened, possibly cloned, project directory. stilo-subagent.js:8 and stilo-prompt.js:45 do the same for SubagentStart and UserPromptSubmit.

Candidate <dir>/.stilo/state.json is accepted with fs.existsSync(p), which follows symlinks. A symlinked .stilo directory or state.json leaf whose target exists is returned as the active path, with no lstat or containment check (same at :108 for the one-level scan).

readStateResult(statePath) reads through the link (readFileSync at :132). A non-JSON target gives status 'unreadable' (:285-286). A JSON object missing the state fields gives 'invalid' (:289-291). statePath keeps the lexical link path.
Shows '- **Arquivo:** <link path>' inside the protected '## Estado do Stilo Code' block, the unresolved in-project-looking path.

Directs the agent: 'Não avance nem aja no projeto até corrigir todos os campos do `state.json`.' The unreadable branch at :217 says 'Corrija o `state.json` antes de agir.', the valid branch at :290 says 'grave você mesmo a fase seguinte em `.stilo/state.json`', and buildStateLine at :176/:183 repeats this on every prompt. The agent's file-write tool is the effect sink.

evidence.description: if (fs.existsSync(p)) return [p]; is the only acceptance test for the discovered state path, and it follows symlinks.

The one-level scan rejects symlinked subdirectories through Dirent.isDirectory(), but it never checks the .stilo component or the state.json leaf. This shows the identity check is partial, not absent by design.
readStateResult reads statePath with fs.readFileSync, following links. There is no lstat, isFile or realpath containment check before the status is decided.
Unreadable branch: 'Não crie nem reinicie o projeto. Corrija o `state.json` antes de agir.' A repair directive for a file whose identity was never checked.
Invalid branch: 'Não avance nem aja no projeto até corrigir todos os campos do `state.json`.' A link to any JSON-object file outside the project reaches it.
Valid branch: 'Ao concluir esta fase, grave você mesmo a fase seguinte em `.stilo/state.json`.'
buildStateLine re-injects 'state.json inválido em <link path> ... não avance nem aja até corrigir o arquivo' on every user prompt.
The only file-type check in the codebase (statSync().isFile()) follows links and is not wired into any hook. Even it would accept a symlink to a regular file outside the project.
The injected ruleset makes writing state.json the agent's responsibility at each phase transition, with no symlink or containment precondition.

blockers: Host write-tool behavior is not source-visible. It is unknown whether Claude Code's Write/Edit tools (and Codex's apply_patch/shell writes) follow a symlink at .stilo/state.json or a symlinked .stilo directory. It is also unknown whether their permission check resolves the real target path, so that a target outside the working directory triggers an out-of-workspace prompt or denial, or uses the lexical in-project path and auto-allows the write.

Checkout behavior is a platform fact. git creates tracked symlinks on POSIX clones, but on Windows only with core.symlinks=true and symlink privilege (Developer Mode or admin). The host here is Windows, where a default clone would check the link out as a plain text file. That gives 'unreadable' with no outside-project write.

Agent behavior is not deterministic. Whether the model, after reading the link target's content (which the tool shows), actually writes or edits the file rather than reporting the anomaly needs an owner-observed run.

No OS-enforced sandbox is available on this host, so no hook or target code was executed. Whether a symlinked state.json reaches the 'invalid' or 'unreadable' injected block was established from source only.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable sandbox (POSIX VM or container, no network, dummy HOME) create /tmp/home/dummy-config.json containing {"keep":true}. Create a project dir with .stilo/state.json as a symlink to /tmp/home/dummy-config.json. Run `node hooks/stilo-activate.js` with cwd set to the project and STILO_HOME pointing to scratch. Confirm the output contains '## Estado do Stilo Code', '**Arquivo:** <project>/.stilo/state.json', '**Estado:** inválido' and 'corrigir todos os campos do `state.json`'. Repeat with the link pointing at a non-JSON dummy file and confirm the 'ilegível' / 'Corrija o `state.json`' block. Regression after the fix: the hook must report the path as refused (symlink or outside the project) and emit no write or repair directive.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, with a dummy HOME. Open a Claude Code session, and separately a Codex session, on a project whose .stilo/state.json is a symlink to a dummy JSON file outside the working directory. Ask the agent to proceed. Record whether the write tool asks for out-of-workspace permission (and which path the prompt names: link or resolved target), denies the write, or modifies the dummy target file. Check whether the dummy file content changed.

hardening: The unwired writer writeJsonAtomic (hooks/stilo-state.js:175-190) uses tmp + renameSync, which replaces a symlinked leaf instead of writing through it. A symlinked .stilo directory would still redirect it, because mkdirSync and the tmp path follow the parent link. If writers are ever wired, add an lstat/realpath containment check on both the .stilo component and the leaf first.

Smallest fix for the candidate: in findStateFiles, accept a candidate only if fs.lstatSync of <dir>/.stilo is a real directory (not a symlink or junction) and fs.lstatSync of state.json isFile() && !isSymbolicLink(), and fs.realpathSync(candidate) starts with fs.realpathSync(dir) + path.sep. Otherwise return a 'refused' diagnosis rendered without any write or repair directive. Regression tests: a symlinked state.json leaf, a symlinked .stilo directory and a junction on Windows must each yield no 'corrigir'/'grave' text.
